key_insight: Evolving molten-zone geometry changes local solidification velocity and helps explain chemical segregation in Ni–Mn–Ga beyond ideal Scheil–Pfann behaviour.
engineering_relevance: Sapphire-confined optical floating-zone growth improves reproducibility and macroscopic shape control, while modelling offers a basis for optimising alloy homogeneity.
method: Grow Ni–Mn–Ga inside a transparent sapphire crucible.
Couple transient COMSOL finite-element heat transfer to an effective molten-zone mass balance.
Compare predicted interfaces and segregation with EBSD and measured composition profiles.
evidence_signal: EBSD of a quenched interface supports the calculated solidification-front geometry, and the coupled model reproduces dominant features of measured composition profiles.
watch_item: The effective mass-balance model is experimentally constrained; quantitative accuracy and transferability to other alloys are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Finite-element reconstruction of molten-zone dynamics and chemical segregation in optical floating-zone grown Ni--Mn--Ga
